correctness.rationale: A nonzero idempotent corresponds bijectively to an F_q-rational fixed point of [v] -> [M v^{[2]}]. The nonzero binary cubic fixed-point equation bounds N by 3. Sharp three-transitivity of PGL_2(F_q) and exact collision counts for projective squaring give factorial moments of orders 1,2,3; inversion yields all four probabilities including p0=1/3. Exhaustive tests over q=2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11 and direct equation checks for q<=5 agree. No asymptotic/infinite conclusion rests on tests.

originality.rationale: The 2026 survey reports the mean number of idempotents and dimension-two existence issues, rather than an identified distribution. A previously accessible variance calculation determines only the first two factorial moments; for odd q, support {0,1,2,3} still leaves the third moment free. The present theorem determines the third factorial moment from noninjectivity of projective squaring, yielding a full histogram and exact one-third idempotent-free frequency. Available full-text 2023 classification concerns isomorphism classes, not the same uniform labeled-matrix statistic. Possible implicit coverage in older projective rational-map or cubic-statistics literature remains a documented risk.
residual_risks: The detailed average-idempotent subsection of arXiv:2610.22248 could not be re-opened after partial HTML access, so unstated coverage there cannot be completely excluded.
The full Wei–Zou paper was not read; its isomorphism counts might imply a related result only after additional counting.
An equivalent probability law for the special rational-map family (a z^2+b)/(c z^2+d), or a classical distribution of binary cubic splitting types, may exist under different terminology.

value.rationale: This gives a complete nontrivial exact distribution for a canonical ensemble motivated by current existence/expectation questions. Exactly one third idempotent-free for every finite field is unexpected field-independence; the odd-characteristic 2-idempotent probability quantifies a genuine collision/degeneracy stratum. The statement is mathematically natural and not a normalization exercise or a restatement of mean/variance.
